messages:
sanjay: Quick proposal — embed a signed `fallback_chain` header inside safetensors so the runtime can pick and hot-swap quant variants without an external manifest. Thoughts?

marta: sketch the header? and how verification works.

sanjay: idea: a small header (first ~4KB) that is JSON with an ordered list of variant entries + routing hints + an RSA/ECDSA signature. Example (conceptual):

```json
{
  "format": "signed_fallback_v1",
  "model_id": "redwood/llama-xyz",
  "variants": [
    {"tag": "fp16", "path": "/blobs/m/123.fp16.safetensors", "latency_hint_ms": "8-12", "cost_score": "1.0"},
    {"tag": "q4_0", "path": "/blobs/m/123.q4_0.safetensors", "latency_hint_ms": "6-9", "cost_score": "0.55"},
    {"tag": "int8", "path": "/blobs/m/123.int8.safetensors", "latency_hint_ms": "7-11", "cost_score": "0.4"}
  ],
  "signature": "BASE64_SIG",
  "signer": "redwood-infra-key-v2"
}
```

sanjay: runtime does `read(0, 4096)` to get header, verify via configured public key (or KMS/HSM), then choose variant by policy. Hot-swap would replace weight pointers to the chosen blob or trigger a staged prefetch.

lee: concerns: 1) backwards compatibility — older loaders should ignore unknown attrs and continue. 2) streaming workflows: sometimes we only stream from object storage and don't read the head; header-first helps but changes streaming semantics. 3) verification cost — signature verify on every start might add latency.

anya: for warmup, how do we avoid double-warmup when switching variants? if we pick q4_0 at routing time but the FP16 KV cache was primed earlier we could lose performance. Need staged warmup: prefetch small subset (embedding + first N layers) for candidate variants, then do fast swap.

ryan: + security note: signature verification must be cached. Suggest: verify on first pull per model_id per node, cache verification result with TTL. Also require offline signing (CI) and move signing keys to HSM.

marta: alternative: keep a tiny sidecar index (manifest object) with the same payload and signature, and embed just a small fingerprint in the safetensors header so streaming clients can `HEAD` the sidecar. Sidecar helps when we use range-requests lazily.

lee: good point. sidecar gives us cheaper mutable mapping (update sidecar without rewriting blobs). But sidecar + embedded fingerprint complicates publish flow.

sanjay: propose hybrid: mandatory 512B fixed header at file start containing format tag + fingerprint + offset to 'meta block'. If loader sees the meta block (streamable), it verifies signature. If not, fallback to sidecar HEAD/GET. This keeps streaming friendly while supporting embedded meta.

anya: warmup plan then: 1) route to variant based on cost/latency hint, 2) prefetch small warmup bundle (first N layers weights) from chosen variant, 3) continue background warmup for full weights. If variant is swapped, we only need to fetch deltas for layers that differ.

ryan: API for loaders: `choose_variant(header, policy)` and `prepare_variant(variant, priming_layers)` — these can be sync fast-path (choose local cache) or async fallback (stream bits).

marta: implementation risks: - increases loader surface area - signature verification library changes - publishing pipeline needs to sign artifacts - tests for partial warmup correctness.

lee: performance question: how big is that header typical? <4KB seems fine. But ensure we don't force whole-file download for small objects in S3 when using range requests. Storing header at fixed offset 0 is good.

sanjay: agree. Also add a `compat` flag per variant so old runtimes can still accept it. Unknown fields should be ignored. Name the scheme `signed_fallback_v1`.

deploy-bot: FYI: infra-ci has a prototype signer job, `signer/prod` queue.

anya: tiny UX ask: when fallback happens in prod, emit a metric `weights.fallback.variant_chosen` + stack sample so we can audit regressions.

marta: +1 to metrics. Also add an eval check: when publishing signed fallback, run a light compare between variants on a couple prompts to ensure quality floor.

lee: action items: Sanjay to open RFC PR with header schema + loader API, Marta to scope publishing pipeline changes, Anya to draft warmup flow, Ryan to write verification caching plan.

sanjay: I'll spin up a short PoC: read-first-4kb, verify signature, parse variants, and return best by policy. Will ping when I have a branch. :rocket:

anya: :thumbsup:

marta: thanks — sounds good.
